item.title: Rumor: Bethesda Has Reportedly Canceled Upcoming Switch 2 Game
item.description:
An upcoming Bethesda game planned for release on the Nintendo Switch 2 has allegedly been canceled, according to a credible insider. Bethesda has already released a handful of titles for Nintendo's latest console, including Switch 2 ports of popular games like The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion Remastered and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle . However, it's beginning to sound less and less likely that a Starfield port ever comes to Switch 2.

The dramatically more powerful Switch 2 has received several third-party ports that would have been nearly impossible on its predecessor. Games like Cyberpunk 2077 , Resident Evil Requiem , and Final Fantasy 7 Remake all showcase just how well the Nintendo console can compete with its PlayStation and Xbox rivals. Even with more impressive hardware, it's still a tall order to get some more graphically intensive games to run on the Switch 2, which may be the case with a Starfield port.

Bethesda Completely Shuts Down New Fallout Game

Bethesda completely shuts down a new Fallout game set in New York City.

By Joshua Duckworth

Insider Claims Starfield Switch 2 Port is Likely Canceled

According to reliable leaker NateTheHate on Twitter, the development of a Starfield Switch 2 port has faced numerous obstacles and has likely been shelved for the time being. Starfield has been rumored to be getting a Switch 2 port since August 2025, with rumors ramping up in March of this year, shortly before the launch of the Starfield PS5 port. However, nothing official was ever announced, and even the rumors of this release have started to die down.

NateTheHate goes on to note that they wouldn't be surprised if the port was canceled entirely, which corroborates what other leakers have said. Despite other large Bethesda RPGs like Oblivion Remastered and Fallout 4 hitting the Switch 2, it's unlikely at this point that Switch 2 port of Starfield will ever see the light of day.

Although Starfield released on PS5 earlier this year along with the Terran Armada expansion and Free Lanes update, interest in Bethesda's spacefaring sci-fi RPG has been waning. Starfield sales on PS5 were reportedly underwhelming, and a former Bethesda developer has gone on record stating they would be very surprised if a Starfield 2 ever happened. Given the alleged development struggles on this Starfield Switch 2 port, it may not be worth the effort to release a game that won't have the audience Bethesda hopes it will on the Switch 2.

Much of Bethesda's attention has likely already shifted away from Starfield and onto other projects as well. Development of The Elder Scrolls 6 is in full swing, with the game said to be targeting a late 2027 or 2028 release window. Bethesda has also doubled down on the Fallout series after treading water with Fallout 76 for years. Remasters of Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas are confirmed to be in development, along with a brand-new Fallout game from Obsidian Entertainment. It's unclear which of these projects will get Nintendo Switch 2 releases, but both The Elder Scrolls and Fallout series have a healthy presence on the console.

item.title: After 16 Years, Forgotten Nintendo DS Game Officially Getting New Release on Steam
item.description:
The Nintendo DS is home to a variety of fan-favorite games, the majority of which are from Nintendo itself. Games like Pokemon HeartGold and SoulSilver , Mario Kart DS , and The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass are typically listed among the handheld's best. However, several third-party Nintendo DS games have quietly been forgotten in the years since the console's heyday, but now one of the best is making a comeback on Steam.

Although the DS is not known for its horror games, the Dementium series is an outlier among the handheld's more beloved titles. The two Dementium games may not be the most celebrated horror games, but they played an important role in the Nintendo DS' history and the greater history of M-rated horror releases on Nintendo consoles. Now, over 15 years after it was originally released, the second Dementium game is getting a new Steam port.

8.7/10 Steam Game is Basically Horror Stardew Valley

A new Steam game is basically a horror version of Stardew Valley, and it is earning very high marks from critics and fans alike.

By Dalton Cooper

Nintendo DS Horror Game Dementium 2 is Getting a New Steam Release

Developer and publisher Atooi has recently launched a Steam page for the classic Nintendo DS horror sequel Dementium 2 , slated for release sometime this month. Although a firm release date hasn't been nailed down, horror fans can expect Dementium 2 to join the lineup of Steam horror games launching in time for the Halloween season. Last year, the first game in the series, Dementium: The Ward , received a Steam port, with its sequel set to follow suit a year later.

The original Dementium 2, restored by the team who made it. William Redmoor wakes with fresh staples in his skull inside an asylum for the criminally insane, where the walls peel back to reveal something worse. Fight, solve, and survive the cult DS horror classic, now on PC.

Dementium 2 follows protagonist William Redmoor, who awakens in Bright Dawn Treatment Center to accusations that he has murdered his wife. William finds himself surrounded by otherworldly horrors as he tries to escape the facility, all while being carefully observed by the man who calls himself the Doctor. Gameplay follows the classic survival horror formula pioneered by games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill , where players will have to solve puzzles, manage their inventory, and fight off horrific creatures if they want to get out alive.

Wishlist Today

The original Dementium was released on the DS in 2007, with this sequel following up on the handheld in 2010. While Dementium 2 did receive an HD Steam release in 2013, development was done by a third-party studio without input from the original developers and was critically panned at release. This new port of Dementium 2 is being handled by the original team to make it as faithful to the Nintendo DS game as possible while offering modern features and graphical upgrades.

Features of this Steam port of Dementium 2 include:

  • Crisp or crunchy. Play in up to 4K, or drop to retro resolution for the pixelated look of the original hardware
  • Classic or modern flashlight. Explore with a realistic new beam, or switch to the original DS stencil light for the authentic look
  • Walk in blind. The original warned you with music whenever an enemy was near. Turn it off, and nothing will tip you off
  • Redesigned for a single screen. Everything the DS split across two displays now fits in one view, with an on-screen mini-map to guide you
  • Your choice of controls: full controller support or mouse and keyboard
  • Plays great on Steam Deck: Take the nightmare to bed with you
  • Steam Achievements to earn
Silent Hill Producer Issues Official Statement on the Series' Future
Rumor: Bethesda Has Reportedly Canceled Upcoming Switch 2 Game
After 16 Years, Forgotten Nintendo DS Game Officially Getting New Release on Steam
Nintendo Switch Online Gamers Have Until October 15 to Play Animal Crossing-Like Game at No Additional Cost

With all the major horror game releases on Steam in October 2026, such as the recently released Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival and Silver Pines , Dementium 2 can't afford to fly under the radar of nostalgic Nintendo DS fans. In the meantime, interested fans can check out Dementium: The Ward on Steam to prepare themselves for the sequel's release later this month.

item.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer: Best Favors Tier List & Combinations
item.description:
There are 20 Favors in Star Wars: Galactic Racer , and we've ranked them all from best to worst. Below, you'll find what every Favor in Star Wars: Galactic Racer does, and discover where they rank so you know which ones to avoid and which ones are worth building into. I've also included the best Favors to use in the Campaign so you know how I managed to beat the game on Championship Difficulty with ease.

All Favors & How to Unlock Them in Star Wars Galactic Racer

Discover all 20 Favors in Star Wars: Galactic Racers and how to unlock them with this complete guide.

By Jake Fillery

Best Favors to Use in a Campaign

My top three Favors are:

  • Fan Club
  • Mad Genius
  • High Roller

Fan Club is essential for ensuring more Vehicle Stat Upgrades, as you'll be finishing each Race and Eliminator with +4 (or sometimes higher) Upgrade Packs.

Mad Genius will also give you added layers of protection against Crashes, which is especially useful on Championship Difficulty when Crashes only return after each planet, not event.

High Roller is perfect for ensuring higher payouts of Credits so I can spend them at Hibi's Shop to get Upgrade Packs and Parts.

All Favors in Star Wars Galactic Racer, Ranked

Favor

Description (Rank 3)

Tier

Fan Club

Upon completing an event in the top 3 positions, 20% chance of gaining a bonus +3 Upgrade Pack.

S-Tier

Mad Genius

Allows 2 extra Crashes per event.

After being Knocked Out, chance to receive 1 additional League Token at the start of the next tour.

S-Tier

Gadgeteer

Increase vehicle Part slots by 2 and increase Parts available at Hibi's Shop by 2.

S-Tier

Earn an additional 100% credits from successful Sidebets.

S-Tier

S-Tier

Part rarity is increased in all Part Packs.

A-Tier

All reward packs include 1 less option, but have a 35% chance of increased reward rarity.

A-Tier

B-Tier

Upon completing an event, each unused Crash awards 200 Credits.

B-Tier

Preferred Customer

Scrap Dealer appears on the map twice as frequently and grants a 50% discount on repairs.

C-Tier

Second Chance

During the first 4 planets, you are protected from losing 1 League Token.

C-Tier

Racer Roulette

Upon winning 4 Biddy Blas Sidebets within a single tour, acquire 1 League Token

C-Tier

Family Legacy

Earn 600 credits for each Takedown achieved on your Rival and 1,200 credits for each on Kestar Bool.

C-Tier

Feet First

Upon completing the first 3 tour events, receive an Ability Pack.

D-Tier

Old Greats

After each successful Podracer Challenge, 100% chance of automatically repairing a Faulty Part.

D-Tier

Bloody Bounty

All reward and shop packs include 2 additional rewards to choose from.

D-Tier

Brutal Calm

Upon completing an event with at least 3 Takedowns achieved, gain +1 Resilience.

D-Tier

Underhanded Upperhand

System Malfunction lasts 10x longer on Sidebet or Head-to-Head opponent.

D-Tier

Clandestine Aid

Begin tour with 1 extra League Token and an additional 2000 credits.

D-Tier

Victorious Loser

Earn 50% increased credit rewards when finishing an event in the bottom 9.

D-Tier

S-Tier: Favors That Make Championship Difficulty a Breeze

  • Fan Club will reward you for coming in the top three spots in Races and Eliminators with a 20% chance to get a +3 Upgrade Pack, on top of the Upgrade Pack you're already getting for completing the event. With Fan Club, you'll end every event with a +4 to your upgrades, which means you'll max your stats in no time.
  • Mad Genius is essential for Championship because you're bound to Crash, so having what's essentially 2 extra lives will really come in clutch when opponents are more aggressive, and you'll need to reach higher speeds to beat them.
  • Gadgeteer will allow you to use 6 Parts instead of just 4, so your vehicle is going to become a monster of potential!
  • High Roller doubles the income from Sidebets, so if you're a risk-taker, you can have enough Credits to upgrade your vehicle at the start of each planet.
  • Unassuming Prodigy will let you start the tour with +2 Upgrades in 3 random Vehicle Stats, which is going to save you Credits.

A-Tier: Favors That Get the Job Done

  • Deeper Pockets makes the reward packs feature 1 less option, but that comes with a 35% chance to increase the reward rarity. If you don't like the part, then skip it for 3,000 Credits, which is more money to spend on other parts.
  • Silent Defiance has a 50% chance to grant you a bonus Part Pack with an increased chance that said Part rarity will be superior. It's not S-Tier because after 4 events, you won't have any room for more Parts.

B-Tier: Underdog Favors

  • Smuggler's Hope will give you a 99% discount on ONE of the Parts in Hibi's Shop, but this Part may be useless.
  • Team Vranki will reward you with 200 Credits for every unused Crash. The extra Credits are nice, but there are so many superior Favors to warrant this one.

C-Tier: The Safety Net Favors

  • Preferred Customer will allow the Scrap Dealer to appear more frequently, which is where you can buy cheap Legendary Parts. You can then repair these Parts for a 50% discount, but it's honestly more trouble than it's worth since you'll have to wait for the next planet to fix them.
  • Second Chance will give you a safety net, as during the first 4 planets, you are protected against losing your first League Token. However, that safety net goes away when you lose, so it's essentially an extra life you don't need since you won't be getting eliminated.
  • Racer Roulette gives you a League Token if you place 4 Sidebets on Biddy Blaz and win, but this requires you to focus on Biddy Blaz and RNG.
  • Family Legacy will give you 600 Credits for each Takedown on your Rival and 1,200 Credits for each Takedown on Kestar Bool. The extra Credits aren't worth going out of your way to take out opponents when you could be winning instead.

D-Tier: The Guaranteed-to-Lose Favors

  • Feet First will give you an Ability Pack after completing three events, but is a cheap Ability worth a Favor? Nope!
  • Old Greats repairs Faulty Parts after Podracer Challenges, but since you're heading to a new planet with the Scrap Dealers anyway, why not just pay for it yourself?
  • Underhanded Upperhand will increase the System Malfunction afflicted on your Sidebet opponent, but if you just race fast, you won't need to go out of your way to cause this.
  • Bloody Bounty increases the reward and shop packs with 2 additional rewards, but you're already spoiled for choice, so skip this one.
  • Brutal Calm will reward you with +1 Resilience if you get 3 Takedowns, but you won't need to play aggressively when Resilience is the one stat you don't need to maximize.
  • Clandestine Aid is pointless, as it only works in Act 1 and Act 2.
  • Victorious Loser is a terrible choice because you will get 50% more Credits if you DON'T finish in the top three, but you'll be losing a League Token anyway, so why make that deal when you can just win and get more Credits (and keep your League Token)?

  • Deeper Pockets makes the reward packs feature 1 less option, but that comes with a 35% chance to increase the reward rarity. If you don't like the part, then skip it for 3,000 Credits, which is more money to spend on other parts.
  • Silent Defiance has a 50% chance to grant you a bonus Part Pack with an increased chance that said Part rarity will be superior. It's not S-Tier because after 4 events, you won't have any room for more Parts.

B-Tier: Underdog Favors

  • Smuggler's Hope will give you a 99% discount on ONE of the Parts in Hibi's Shop, but this Part may be useless.
  • Team Vranki will reward you with 200 Credits for every unused Crash. The extra Credits are nice, but there are so many superior Favors to warrant this one.

C-Tier: The Safety Net Favors

  • Preferred Customer will allow the Scrap Dealer to appear more frequently, which is where you can buy cheap Legendary Parts. You can then repair these Parts for a 50% discount, but it's honestly more trouble than it's worth since you'll have to wait for the next planet to fix them.
  • Second Chance will give you a safety net, as during the first 4 planets, you are protected against losing your first League Token. However, that safety net goes away when you lose, so it's essentially an extra life you don't need since you won't be getting eliminated.
  • Racer Roulette gives you a League Token if you place 4 Sidebets on Biddy Blaz and win, but this requires you to focus on Biddy Blaz and RNG.
  • Family Legacy will give you 600 Credits for each Takedown on your Rival and 1,200 Credits for each Takedown on Kestar Bool. The extra Credits aren't worth going out of your way to take out opponents when you could be winning instead.

D-Tier: The Guaranteed-to-Lose Favors

  • Feet First will give you an Ability Pack after completing three events, but is a cheap Ability worth a Favor? Nope!
  • Old Greats repairs Faulty Parts after Podracer Challenges, but since you're heading to a new planet with the Scrap Dealers anyway, why not just pay for it yourself?
  • Underhanded Upperhand will increase the System Malfunction afflicted on your Sidebet opponent, but if you just race fast, you won't need to go out of your way to cause this.
  • Bloody Bounty increases the reward and shop packs with 2 additional rewards, but you're already spoiled for choice, so skip this one.
  • Brutal Calm will reward you with +1 Resilience if you get 3 Takedowns, but you won't need to play aggressively when Resilience is the one stat you don't need to maximize.
  • Clandestine Aid is pointless, as it only works in Act 1 and Act 2.
  • Victorious Loser is a terrible choice because you will get 50% more Credits if you DON'T finish in the top three, but you'll be losing a League Token anyway, so why make that deal when you can just win and get more Credits (and keep your League Token)?

item.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Release Date Gives Its Campaign One Week to Actually Matter
item.description:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is one of the biggest launches scheduled for October, and it's one of the last major games before the likes of Nintendo's Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6 come blazing through to overshadow everything else. This release date puts Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in a fascinating position, and the campaign launching ahead of the rest of the game adds even more intrigue to the franchise's newest Modern Warfare chapter. Modern Warfare 4 is a completely original story that marks the series' departure from the original trilogy and its reboot. Set during a modern-day conflict between North and South Korea, there are some high expectations surrounding the game, and its newness makes the campaign far more compelling than the last three chapters.

This time around, Modern Warfare 4 finally gets to tell a brand-new story within the Modern Warfare timeline. Every Modern Warfare game has had its own unique story to tell, but Modern Warfare 4 's new setting presents a fresh era for the Call of Duty spin-off. Between Mads Mikkelsen playing Modern Warfare 4 's villain and Captain John Price going rogue, this campaign could be one of Call of Duty 's best in a long time, and getting to experience it before actual launch gives it a much-deserved spotlight.

CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Is Officially the Largest Campaign in MW History

During a chat with GameRant about Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward confirmed its campaign as the largest in the series' history.

4
By Josh Cotts

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Campaign Early Access Is a Pre-Order Bonus Worth Celebrating

Pre-order bonuses for games are obviously nothing new, but a lot of these rewards feel more like publishers and developers are ticking off a box on a to-do list instead of actually bringing anything meaningful to players. For example, God of War Laufey is one of my most-anticipated games at the moment, but the pre-order rewards haven't convinced me to purchase early. The God of War Laufey pre-order bonuses for the Standard Edition are just in-game skins for the most part, while Modern Warfare 4 lets fans dive into the campaign an entire week early. One reward type clearly outshines the other.

Seconds

This Is When Modern Warfare 4's Campaign Early Access Goes Live

  • Campaign Early Access goes live on October 16.
  • Campaign Early Access is only for pre-orders .
  • Multiplayer and DMZ will be released on October 23.

Granted, this is far from the first time that a pre-order bonus has included early access. Games like LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight have offered three-day early access as an incentive to buy early, but Activision offering an entire week is a great move that is bound to give the campaign some serious time to shine. Modern Warfare 4 's campaign early access might not be as exciting for fans who are multiplayer die-hards, but it's the necessary appetizer to ignite extra hype ahead of the full launch.

Modern Warfare 4's Early Access Can Hopefully Break the Current Call of Duty Campaign Curse

The past few years of Call of Duty campaigns have seen a lot of highs and lows. Whether it's Black Ops 6 and Cold War 's stronger stories or Modern Warfare 3 and Black Ops 7 's letdowns, they all have something in common: they immediately get overlooked by multiplayer. This really isn't a surprise or anything. Multiplayer has always been part of the Call of Duty identity, but it has evolved into a completely different beast since the franchise's early days.

This campaign could be one of Call of Duty 's best in a long time.

Even when the games feature strong campaigns, the discourse surrounding multiplayer sucks up all the air in the room. The Call of Duty franchise needs to make its campaigns truly matter again, and Modern Warfare 4 may have found the key to making that happen, at least for a short while. Now that there's the added element of Modern Warfare 4 's DMZ mode being thrown into the mix, it would be even harder for the campaign to stand out on October 23.

Modern Warfare 4's Campaign Has the Chance to Usher in a New Call of Duty Era

The hit-and-miss nature of each Call of Duty campaign has kept a lot of players wary about jumping into every new game's story mode. That's understandable, especially when they tend to be so short. Story length is one of the things that made Modern Warfare 3 such a controversial entry. Modern Warfare 3 's short campaign takes less than five hours to complete. Such a short length makes it really hard to get invested in a story that's supposed to be an action-packed and thrilling look inside military operations.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Release Date Gives Its Campaign One Week to Actually Matter
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Just Revealed the Best Reason Yet to Loot Everything in DMZ
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's New DMZ Is Borrowing the One Thing Extraction Shooters Can't Fake
CoD Modern Warfare 4: Should You Buy the Vault Edition?

Modern Warfare 4 's story can hopefully turn things around, though. The new entry has the pressure of righting Modern Warfare 3 's wrongs, and with three years between releases, Infinity Ward has theoretically had enough time to craft a stronger narrative. Modern Warfare 4 being a completely new chapter also has its benefits, because it doesn't have to live up to the expectations set by the original trilogy. It's uncharted territory for the Modern Warfare games, and that might be just what the series needed all along.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

item.title: 6-Year-Old Designed Pokemon Card That Sold for $156,000
item.description:
A Pokemon card featuring artwork of Zorua that was drawn by a 6-year-old fan from Japan was sold at a late September auction for an eye-catching price of $156,000. The Pokemon card that was sold for six figures was just one of approximately a hundred cards that were printed in limited quantities.

Although the Pokemon Trading Card Game remains a popular hobby for fans and collectible enthusiasts alike, the game has also drawn the attention of scalpers. As Pokemon TCG products continue to fly off the shelves to be resold for ridiculous prices, fans have called on The Pokemon Company and retailers to intervene. In response, Target staff members have removed the seals from Elite Trainer Boxes as a way to drive down the resale value of the products in question, which may deter scalpers trying to make a profit.

New Pokemon LEGO Release Leaked

A new LEGO Pokemon option leaks online ahead of an official announcement, and it should be exciting news for fans of the franchise.

By Marc Deschamps

Rare Zorua Pokemon Card Fetches $156,000 at Auction

While some Pokemon cards are known for featuring eye-catching artwork, one fan's contribution to the series fetched a high price at a late auction. A Zorua card that featured artwork drawn by then-six-year-old Megu Taniguchi was sold through Fanatics Collect for $156,000 at an auction that closed on September 27. The card was graded as PSA 10 Gem Mint and had 38 bids. Only 100 copies of the Zorua promo card featuring Taniguchi's artwork were printed, which added value to the card in question. Taniguchi's drawing depicted Zorua riding on a red bus alongside Pikachu and another individual. The drawing was made as part of a 2010 contest to celebrate the theatrical release of the Pokemon anime movie Zoroark: Master of Illusions in Japan. Ergo, both the card and artwork are 16 years old as of this writing. Taniguchi was chosen as the Kindergarten Winner of the promotion and received both prize money and a small print run of the cards she drew art for.

Since the Zorua card was released as part of a promotion, it was never included in traditional Pokemon TCG booster packs. However, it is unclear if the card that was sold for $156,000 was from Taniguchi's prize print or through another print run altogether. Though the PSA 10 Gem Mint Zorua card fetched a high price, a separate auction featuring Raincoat Pikachu sold for $8.4 million through Fanatics Collect on the same day with 84 bids. In short, selling high-grade Pokemon cards continues to be a lucrative endeavor for all involved.
